deck.title: SQS, SNS & Kinesis
deck.analogy: SQS is a mailbox (letters wait until collected), SNS is a megaphone (everyone hears it now, then it's gone), Kinesis is a river (many read the same water and you can wade back to re-read).

subtopics.title: SQS — the mailbox (queue, PULL, one message → ONE worker)
Kinesis Data Firehose — the delivery truck

cards.front: Why put an SQS queue between a web tier and an order processor?

back.answer: It decouples them: instant response, messages survive crashes, and spikes lengthen the queue instead of killing the worker.
back.explanation: Direct sync calls cause spinners, lost orders and overload.
back.mnemonic: SQS is a mailbox: letters wait until you collect them.

cards.front: SQS vs SNS vs Kinesis: what is each analogy?

back.answer: SQS = mailbox, SNS = megaphone, Kinesis = river.
back.explanation: Mailbox holds letters until collected; megaphone is heard now then gone; river is readable by many and replayable.

cards.front: How does SQS deliver messages: push or pull, and to how many workers?

back.answer: Consumers PULL; each message is processed by exactly one worker.
back.explanation: Once someone takes the letter from the mailbox, it's theirs.

cards.sourceHeading: SQS — the mailbox (queue, PULL, one message → ONE worker)

cards.front: What does the SQS visibility timeout do when a worker reads a message?

back.answer: The message is hidden, not deleted (default 30 seconds); if not deleted in time it reappears.
back.explanation: Worker deletes it when finished; if it crashes, the message reappears for another worker — built-in retry.

cards.sourceHeading: SQS — the mailbox (queue, PULL, one message → ONE worker)

cards.front: What is the default SQS visibility timeout?

back.answer: 30 seconds.

cards.sourceHeading: SQS — the mailbox (queue, PULL, one message → ONE worker)

cards.front: SQS messages are being processed twice. What is the cause and fix?

back.answer: Processing outlasts the visibility timeout, so the message reappears; increase the visibility timeout.
back.explanation: Message becomes visible again while worker #1 is still processing it.

cards.sourceHeading: SQS — the mailbox (queue, PULL, one message → ONE worker)

cards.front: What is an SQS Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ)?

back.answer: A side queue where a poison message is moved after MaxReceiveCount failed attempts.
back.explanation: Lets you inspect failures without clogging the main queue.

cards.sourceHeading: SQS — the mailbox (queue, PULL, one message → ONE worker)

cards.front: What is SQS long polling and when do you use it?

back.answer: Consumer waits up to 20 seconds for messages; use it to reduce cost and empty responses.
back.explanation: Avoids hammering with empty-poll requests.

cards.sourceHeading: SQS — the mailbox (queue, PULL, one message → ONE worker)

cards.front: What is the SQS max message size and how do you handle larger payloads?

back.answer: 256 KB; store the payload in S3 and send a pointer in the message.

cards.sourceHeading: SQS — the mailbox (queue, PULL, one message → ONE worker)

cards.front: What are SQS message retention default and maximum?

back.answer: 4 days default, 14 days maximum.
back.explanation: Not a database — collect your mail.

cards.sourceHeading: SQS — the mailbox (queue, PULL, one message → ONE worker)

cards.front: SQS Standard vs FIFO: throughput?

back.answer: Standard: unlimited. FIFO: 300 msg/s (3,000 with batching).

cards.sourceHeading: SQS — the mailbox (queue, PULL, one message → ONE worker)

cards.front: SQS Standard vs FIFO: delivery guarantee?

back.answer: Standard: at-least-once (duplicates possible). FIFO: exactly-once.

cards.sourceHeading: SQS — the mailbox (queue, PULL, one message → ONE worker)

cards.front: SQS Standard vs FIFO: ordering?

back.answer: Standard: best-effort order. FIFO: strict order.

cards.sourceHeading: SQS — the mailbox (queue, PULL, one message → ONE worker)

cards.front: When do you choose SQS Standard vs FIFO?

back.answer: Standard is the default choice; FIFO when "order matters" or "no duplicates".

cards.sourceHeading: SQS — the mailbox (queue, PULL, one message → ONE worker)

cards.front: What is the classic SQS worker scaling pattern?

back.answer: Auto Scaling Group of workers scaling on queue depth via CloudWatch ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible.
back.explanation: The queue gets long, more workers spawn.

cards.sourceHeading: SQS — the mailbox (queue, PULL, one message → ONE worker)

cards.front: What is SNS and who can be subscribers?

back.answer: Publish to a topic; SNS PUSHES to all subscribers: Lambda, SQS, HTTP, email, SMS, mobile push.
back.mnemonic: Megaphone: everyone in earshot hears it now.

cards.front: What happens in SNS if a subscriber is down when a message is published?

back.answer: It misses the message; SNS stores nothing.
back.explanation: Megaphone, not mailbox. Fan out into SQS when reliability matters.

cards.front: What does SNS message filtering do?

back.answer: A filter policy per subscription lets each subscriber receive only matching messages.
back.explanation: E.g., billing gets only order_type: refund.

cards.front: What is the SNS fan-out pattern and why use SQS behind SNS?

back.answer: SNS topic → multiple SQS queues; queues hold messages durably if a consumer is down.
back.explanation: Never SNS alone when reliability matters.

cards.front: What two superpowers does Kinesis Data Streams have that SQS lacks?

back.answer: Multiple consumers read the SAME data, and REPLAY of retained data.
back.explanation: Retention is 24 hours default, up to 365 days.
back.mnemonic: River: many on the bank, wade upstream to re-read.

cards.front: What is Kinesis Data Streams retention?

back.answer: 24 hours default, up to 365 days.

cards.front: What is a Kinesis Data Streams shard's capacity and ordering?

back.answer: 1 MB/s in, 2 MB/s out; ordering guaranteed per shard (partition key picks shard).
back.explanation: More throughput = more shards.

cards.front: Keyword: **"reprocess yesterday's data"** or **"two applications must read the same stream"**

back.answer: Kinesis Data Streams, never SQS.

cards.front: What are the key traits of Kinesis Data Firehose?

back.answer: Near-real-time (~60s buffering), zero code, fully managed; delivers to S3, Redshift, OpenSearch, Splunk, optional Lambda transform.

cards.sourceHeading: Kinesis Data Firehose — the delivery truck

cards.front: Firehose vs Kinesis Data Streams: when each?

back.answer: Firehose for stream into S3 with least effort/no code; Streams if custom consumers or replay needed.

cards.sourceHeading: Kinesis Data Firehose — the delivery truck

cards.front: When do you choose Amazon MQ?

back.answer: Migrating an app using MQTT, AMQP, JMS or STOMP (RabbitMQ/ActiveMQ) without code changes.
back.explanation: Managed RabbitMQ/ActiveMQ enables lift-and-shift.

cards.front: SQS: model, consumers, storage, pick-when?

back.answer: Queue, PULL; ONE consumer per message; 4–14 days, no replay after delete; decouple, buffer spikes, distribute work.

cards.front: SNS: model, consumers, storage, pick-when?

back.answer: Pub/sub PUSH; MANY at once; no storage; notify many instantly (fan out to SQS for durability).

cards.front: Kinesis Data Streams: model, consumers, storage, pick-when?

back.answer: Stream; MANY read SAME data; 24h–365d replayable; real-time analytics, multiple readers, reprocessing.

cards.front: Firehose: model, consumers, storage, pick-when?

back.answer: Delivery pipe; fixed destinations; buffers ~60s; dump streams to S3/Redshift/OpenSearch/Splunk with zero code.

cards.front: Amazon MQ: model, consumers, storage, pick-when?

back.answer: Traditional broker; protocol-based consumers; broker semantics; MQTT/AMQP/JMS migration with no code changes.

cards.front: A web tier is overwhelmed by traffic spikes and orders are being lost. Which design fits?

back.answer: SQS plus an Auto Scaling worker group.
back.explanation: Queue buffers the spike; workers scale on depth.

choices.text: SQS queue with Auto Scaling workers
choices.why: Queue buffers spikes; workers scale on depth.

cards.front: Messages must be processed in strict order with no duplicates. Which service?

back.answer: SQS FIFO.
back.explanation: Order plus exactly-once; capped at 300/3,000 msg/s.

cards.front: One event must notify three downstream systems, and none may miss it even if temporarily down.

back.answer: SNS fan-out to multiple SQS queues.
back.explanation: Queues hold messages for sleeping services.

choices.text: SNS topic with direct HTTP subscribers

choices.why: Each message goes to only one worker.

choices.text: SNS topic fanning out to multiple SQS queues
choices.why: Queues durably hold messages per consumer.

cards.front: Some SQS messages are being processed twice. What do you do?

back.answer: Increase the visibility timeout.
back.explanation: Processing outlasts the hiding window.

cards.front: Messages that repeatedly fail are blocking the SQS queue. Fix?

back.answer: Dead-Letter Queue with MaxReceiveCount.
back.explanation: Quarantines poison messages.

choices.why: Moves poison messages aside after N attempts.

cards.front: Clickstream analytics: two applications must consume the same real-time data, and yesterday's data must be reprocessable.

back.answer: Kinesis Data Streams.
back.explanation: Multiple consumers plus replay.

choices.why: One consumer per message, no replay.

cards.front: Stream IoT telemetry into S3 with least operational overhead and no custom code.

back.answer: Kinesis Data Firehose.
back.explanation: Zero-code delivery truck to S3.

choices.text: Kinesis Data Streams with custom consumers

choices.why: Fully managed, zero code to S3.

cards.front: Reduce the cost of consumers polling an often-empty SQS queue.

back.answer: Long polling (20s).
back.explanation: Fewer empty receives.

choices.why: Waits up to 20s, fewer empty responses.

cards.front: Migrate an on-prem RabbitMQ/ActiveMQ app using AMQP/JMS/MQTT without rewriting.

back.answer: Amazon MQ.
back.explanation: Protocol names signal Amazon MQ.

cards.front: Message payloads are 1 MB, exceeding the SQS limit. What do you do?

back.answer: Store in S3, send a pointer.
back.explanation: SQS caps at 256 KB.

choices.text: Raise the SQS size limit to 1 MB
Store payload in S3 and send a pointer

cards.front: Each subscriber should only receive certain message types from an SNS topic.

back.answer: SNS message filtering.
back.explanation: Filter policy per subscription.

choices.text: Lambda filter in front of SQS
choices.why: Extra code; SNS does this natively.

cards.front: Keyword: **"Decouple / buffer spikes"**

back.answer: SQS

cards.front: Keyword: **"One message → one worker, PULL"**

back.answer: SQS

cards.front: Keyword: **"Processed twice"**

back.answer: Increase visibility timeout (default 30s)

cards.front: Keyword: **"Poison messages"**

back.answer: DLQ + MaxReceiveCount

cards.front: Keyword: **"Empty-poll cost"**

back.answer: Long polling (20s)

cards.front: Keyword: **"Strict order + exactly-once"**

back.answer: FIFO (300 / 3,000 msg/s)

cards.front: Keyword: **"Message > 256 KB"**

back.answer: S3 + pointer

cards.front: Keyword: **"Retention"** (SQS)

back.answer: 4 days default / 14 max

cards.front: Keyword: **"One → many, PUSH, instant"**

back.answer: SNS (stores nothing)

cards.front: Keyword: **"Notify many, durably"**

back.answer: SNS → multiple SQS (fan-out)

cards.front: Keyword: **"Multiple consumers, same data, replay"**

back.answer: Kinesis Data Streams (24h–365d)

cards.front: Keyword: **"Shard throughput"**

back.answer: 1 MB/s in, 2 MB/s out, order per shard

cards.front: Keyword: **"Stream → S3, zero code, ~60s"**

back.answer: Firehose (S3/Redshift/OpenSearch/Splunk)

cards.front: Keyword: **"MQTT / AMQP / JMS / RabbitMQ"**

back.answer: Amazon MQ

cards.front: Keyword: **"Workers scale on queue depth"**

back.answer: ASG + CloudWatch queue metric
